data.title: AFC reports lower revenue and reduced interim loss
data.description:
AFC Group Holdings Limited ( (NZ:AFC) ) has provided an update.

AFC Group Holdings Limited’s reported revenue comes from cosmetic and wine products, and its businesses include biotechnology manufacturing. Longview Estate maintained vineyard and wine inventories, while AFC Biotechnology Manufacture Co Limited generated limited sales from existing stock and had largely unutilised manufacturing capacity before ceasing operations after the period end.

For the six months ended 30 September 2026, operating revenue was NZ$19,723, down from NZ$33,053, and the net loss was NZ$282,476, compared with NZ$363,640 a year earlier. The group had net liabilities of NZ$76,086, current liabilities exceeding current assets, and a disclosed material uncertainty related to going concern; no dividend was proposed.

data.title: Torrent Capital Reports Preliminary October NAV and Portfolio Update
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Torrent Capital Ltd ( (TSE:TORR) ).

Torrent Capital reported preliminary, unaudited October 2026 results showing estimated NAV of approximately $26.3 million, or $0.69 per share, as of October 31, compared with approximately $28.6 million, or $0.75 per share, as of September 30. Cash and cash equivalents increased to $7.3 million from $4.7 million over the same period.

Management said October market weakness, which persisted into November, weighed on portfolio valuations. The October financial information is preliminary and unaudited and remains subject to change following the company’s standard closing procedures and review.

data.title: Abcourt Reports First-Quarter Results With C$7.0 Million Gold Revenue
data.description:
Abcourt Mines ( (TSE:ABI) ) has shared an update.

Abcourt Mines, a Canadian gold company developing the Sleeping Giant mine and mill and exploring its Flordin property in northwestern Quebec, reported first-quarter results for the period ended September 30, 2026. It sold 1,155 ounces of gold at an average realized price of C$5,848 per ounce, generating C$7.0 million in revenue, compared with no revenue in the year-earlier quarter.

Costs of sales were C$16.8 million and net loss was C$13.2 million, compared with a C$7.5 million loss in the prior-year quarter. Abcourt increased its Glencore senior secured debenture to US$40 million, had drawn US$38 million by September 30, and repaid its Nebari facility in full in September; cash was C$1.4 million and working capital was C$1.9 million at quarter-end.

data.title: New Zealand Consumer Confidence Surges Past Expectations
data.description:
New Zealand’s ANZ Roy Morgan Consumer Confidence rose to 100.2 from 96.2, an increase of 4.0 points, or about 4.2%. The reading moved higher and returned above the 100 threshold.

The result exceeded the analyst estimate of 96.5 by 3.7 points, or about 3.8%, signaling firmer consumer sentiment than expected. Retailers and consumer-discretionary stocks are likely to benefit from improved demand expectations, while the broader market impact should be short-term and sentiment-driven.

data.title: ARSESP Validates Sabesp’s 2025 Regulatory Asset Base at R$97.8 Billion
data.description:
Companhia de Saneamento Basico do Estado de Sao Paulo SABESP ( (BR:SBSP3) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Sabesp said São Paulo’s public-services regulator, ARSESP, validated its 2025 Regulatory Asset Base at R$97.8 billion, measured at December 2025 values. The figure rose from a protected RAB of R$88.0 billion at December 2024, incorporating R$10.9 billion in gross additions, R$4.0 billion of inflation and R$3.8 billion in depreciation.

Other adjustments included R$0.6 billion in asset write-offs, R$0.2 billion in photovoltaic solar investments and R$0.3 billion representing the difference between JOA and JOAR. Sabesp said the written-off assets had been in service but were no longer operating, while the solar investments were not recognized in the 2024 and 2025 RAB.

data.title: Warehouse Group reports FY26 operating profit recovery
data.description:
Warehouse Group ( (NZ:WHS) ) has provided an update.

At its 2026 annual meeting, the group reported FY26 sales of $3,027.6m, down 1.9% on the 53-week FY25, while comparable 52-week sales fell 0.2% and same-store sales rose 0.4%. Operating profit increased to $22.6m from $1.3m as gross margin rose to 32.6% and cost of doing business fell 3.0%.

Free cash flow was $79.4m and net debt declined by $79.1m to $17.0m, while the group increased investment in its store network. Noel Leeming and Warehouse Stationery delivered stronger returns, but the company said The Warehouse remained below an acceptable profitability level and was its most important recovery priority; no final dividend was declared for FY26.

data.title: Fab-Form Reports USPTO Allowance for SPACE-R Patent Claims
data.description:
Fab-Form ( (TSE:FBF) ) has provided an announcement.

Fab-Form Industries Ltd., a Vancouver, British Columbia-based manufacturer of eco-friendly concrete forming products, develops foundation products for the building industry and has traded on the TSX Venture Exchange under FBF since 2000. The company announced that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has allowed patent claims for SPACE-R, its concrete-column reinforcement product, describing the allowance as a milestone.

SPACE-R replaces a traditional horizontal steel stirrup with a lightweight fiberglass component, uses polypropylene clips to connect vertical rebar, and has polypropylene fins to position reinforcement in column forms. The company says the design reduces shipping costs and onsite labor while addressing corrosion and installation-error concerns, and that it works with contractors’ existing formwork and Fab-Form’s Fast-Tube fabric form.

data.title: NiobiumX Describes Shipshaw Niobium Exploration Methodology
data.description:
Arctic Fox Ventures ( (TSE:NIOX) ) just unveiled an announcement.

NiobiumX described an exploration methodology combining airborne magnetic data, ground radiometric data, structural mapping and machine learning. The approach focuses on magnetic lows, thorium highs and geological structures associated with carbonatite systems that can host niobium mineralization.

Historical drilling tested 23 holes in the northern part of the Shipshaw magnetic low, intersecting carbonatite in 21, while the centre of the anomaly remains undrilled. The release says machine learning will compare Shipshaw’s geophysical characteristics with the nearby Saint-Honoré complex and help rank areas for drilling and assay.
